title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Arcadia Health
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on Arcadia's plan to extend contract 12-18 months, add dedicated capacity in US + EU and pilot APAC region. Discussed options for committed reserved capacity vs burst/hosted, compliance docs, and next steps for pricing and PO.
next_steps: Jordan to send updated pricing for 12- and 18-month committed options (by 2027-09-15)
Maya to share benchmark runbook and sample workload for Arcadia to run in their staging (by 2027-09-13)
Sofia to attach SOC 2 report and updated data residency whitepaper (by 2027-09-10)
Arcadia to confirm preferred regions and prelim committed vGPU counts (by 2027-09-20)
Schedule procurement intro with Ryan from Redwood finance (if Arcadia goes forward) (proposed 2027-09-21)
action_items: Jordan - Send 12/18 month committed pricing + examples of unit economics (due 2027-09-15)
Maya - Share benchmark artifacts (script + sample payloads) and runbook (due 2027-09-13)

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-09-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reed (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Torres (Redwood CSM), Tom Chen (Arcadia Head of ML), Priya Singh (VP Eng), Liam O'Connor (Infra Lead), Rosa Medina (Procurement)

Summary (auto): Renewal + expansion check-in; capacity add + region expansion; pricing options discussed; SOC 2 & residency docs requested.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, then we'll get into renewal and the capacity asks.
[00:15] Tom (Arcadia): Hey, Tom here. thanks.
[00:18] Priya (Arcadia): Priya here.
[00:22] Liam (Arcadia): Liam here.
[00:25] Rosa (Arcadia): Rosa — procurement.
[00:29] Jordan: Great. Maya and Sofia from our side too. We'll keep this to about 40 minutes.

[01:05] Jordan: To frame, your current contract is up in mid-Oct, right? We wanted to go over options — 12 vs 18 month commit, adding dedicated capacity in us-west + eu-west, and pilot in apac. Tom, is that the right set?
[01:22] Tom: Yeah that's right. current usage has ramped more than we expected. spikes during end-of-month reconciliation have been rough. median latencies okay but p95 is getting pricy.
[01:38] Maya (Redwood SE): When you say p95 pricy, is that mostly because requests are hitting hosted bursting rates or because KV cache misses?
[01:48] Tom: It's a combo — we saw a lot of cold starts and also KV cache misses when models shift across shards. sometimes the cache invalidates when we reroute between regions — maybe our routing config is naive.
[02:05] Liam: also a note: our infra team wants more predictable unit costs. The variance hurts forecasting.

[02:30] Jordan: Ok, dedicated reserved capacity is the levers there. committed vGPU pools give you stable throughput and lower unit price. We outlined two tiers — small reserved pool vs large. The big one gets you better per-token and lower queuing.
[02:52] Priya: can you give rough numbers? we need to compare to our internal on-prem run costs (we're also evaluating Vertex and Anthropic tethered options).
[03:04] Jordan: Totally. I'll send a side-by-side for 12 vs 18 month commit and the on-demand hosted pricing, includes typical autoscale/burst. short answer: 18 month committed is ~25% cheaper per token vs on-demand, and dedicated plus prefix caching reduces effective compute by about 20% on many workloads.
[03:28] Priya: good. how does the capacity expansion timeline look if we add EU region?
[03:36] Maya: For EU-1 we can stand up dedicated pools within 2-3 weeks once the commit and onboarding paperwork is in. APAC is slightly longer because of region availability and infra scheduling — think 4-6 weeks for a pilot.
[03:50] Tom: Are there data residency implications? we must keep PHI in-region for some workflows.
[03:57] Sofia (Redwood CSM): We have region-level controls and data residency guarantees in the enterprise addendum. we'll share the data residency whitepaper. That covers encryption at rest, KMS usage and regional data egress policies.
[04:14] Priya: can you confirm KMS/HSM support? we use Azure Key Vault and AWS KMS for different workloads.
[04:22] Maya: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS in both AWS and Azure; we also integrate with on-prem HSMs for private deployments. small caveat: some older model snapshots need re-encryption step during onboarding, we document that.
[04:37] Liam: how about SSO and RBAC? our security folks will want SCIM + SAML and fine-grained roles.
[04:44] Jordan: SSO, SCIM, SAML, and org-level RBAC are part of our enterprise plan. Sofia will share the security pack and an example RBAC role matrix.

[05:10] Tom: On the benchmark side, we want to run our typical batch inference (30k reqs/day with bursts) and compare latency and cost across on-prem vs Redwood dedicated. what's the plan?
[05:22] Maya: We'll provide a benchmark runbook — includes sample payloads, data scrubbing steps, and scripts to replay traffic. ideally you run in staging against the dedicated pool we provision or you can run locally using our dockerized runner.
[05:38] Tom: We prefer Redwood to run an initial benchmark if you can, then we'll replay on our side.
[05:43] Maya: That's doable — we'll need a short-lived test account and agreed traffic windows. we'll also instrument token-level traces.

[06:05] Jordan: Procurement note: Rosa, what timeline would you need to sign a 12 vs 18 month contract?
[06:12] Rosa: For procurement to process a PO for a committed amount we'd need pricing and SOW by next Friday ideally; procurement sign-off typically takes 7-10 business days. If you can get an initial quote by 9/15 that's good.
[06:26] Jordan: We'll do that. I'll prepare 12 and 18 month options with expected committed vGPU counts and a representative unit econ spreadsheet.

[06:45] Priya: One technical question — if we add dedicated pools in EU, will we need separate model variants or can we use the same model version pinned across regions?
[06:56] Maya: You can use the same model version. we support pinning models and consistent rollouts. small caveat: we may use different micro-optimizations (quantization profile / kernel selection) by hardware family per region, but semantics stay the same. sometimes model perf differs by a few milliseconds due to kernel scheduling.
[07:19] Tom: That difference can matter for p99 for us. can you surface per-region latency dash so our SREs can monitor?
[07:27] Sofia: Yes — per-route/per-region dashboards and tracing are available. we can add an alert recipe for p95/p99 regressions tied to your eval prompts.

[08:00] Liam: about failover — if EU pool is down, can requests route to US with data residency flags? is there an audit trail?
[08:09] Maya: We support smart routing with policy-based fallback. for data residency constrained flows, you can set hard fail — so requests won't leave region — or soft fallback. all routing actions are logged and we provide audit logs and request-level traces.
[08:23] Jordan: in practice, for PHI you probably want hard fail. we'll note that in the config.

[08:40] Priya: Pricing question — what does a committed pool incremental add look like mid-contract? we might expand in quarter 2 next year.
[08:50] Jordan: We support add-on commits; pricing for additional commits mid-term is pro-rated and often uses the same committed rates if you reach the threshold. We can include flexible burst buckets on top.

[09:15] Tom: Competitor question: we've been doing some benchmarking with Anthropic and OpenAI's hosted endpoints; how do you compare on cost for embeddings-heavy workloads?
[09:26] Maya: For embeddings, dedicated pools with optimized kernels and batching/kv caching are typically cheaper by 30-40% compared to general hosted endpoints at scale. but it depends on model choice and batch patterns. we'll attach a worked example.

[09:50] Rosa: For procurement, we'll need a sample SOW and the invoicing cadence. can you do monthly invoices with quarterly true-ups?
[10:00] Jordan: Yes we can offer monthly invoices. Sofia will include invoicing cadence options in the quote, including monthly with quarterly reconciliations.

[10:25] Priya: A few small details from security: SOC 2 expiration date, evidence of penetration test, and segmentation between shared control plane and private workloads.
[10:36] Sofia: We'll share SOC 2 report and recent pen test summary. Our architecture doc calls out control plane separation for private deployments — we'll share the whitepaper.

[11:00] Tom: On the technical ops side, can we get CLI access and service accounts for batch runners?
[11:06] Maya: Yes — service keys and least-privilege roles are supported. we recommend scoped service accounts for batch jobs.

[11:25] Jordan: Recap — action items: we'll send pricing and contract options by 9/15, security docs by 9/10, benchmark runbook by 9/13. Arcadia to confirm region + vGPU counts by 9/20. Sofia will open a shared folder for docs.

[11:45] Tom: quick question: if we do a pilot in APAC and like it, how quickly can we scale to production there?
[11:52] Maya: Once pilot confirms perf, scaling to production depends on capacity scheduling; typically 4-8 weeks for production-grade pools in APAC given GPU availability.

[12:10] Priya: One more — pricing floor for committed vs on-demand for long tail inference?
[12:17] Jordan: We'll show a blended example in the spreadsheet. committed pools handle the majority and on-demand for unexpected spikes; effective blended rate is usually quoted.

[12:35] Rosa: Procurement question — are there pre-approved T&C's or will legal need to review full master services agreement?
[12:41] Jordan: For enterprise we'll provide our standard MSA and an enterprise addendum. legal tends to review; we'll mark up common clauses up front to accelerate.

[13:00] Tom: Sounds good. we'll look for the docs.
[13:04] Jordan: Thanks everyone. any other Qs?
[13:08] Priya: none from me.
[13:10] Liam: all good.
[13:12] Rosa: Nope.

[13:20] Jordan: Great — we'll follow up on the timeline and send the pricing by 9/15. thanks all.

[13:30] (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mislabels, small transcription errors ("KV cash" vs "KV cache", "V-B-C" vs "VPC"), speaker overlaps, and run-on lines retained to preserve meeting artifact feel.
